design_philosophy: Operator-focused dashboard aesthetic designed for fast-paced restaurant environments. Prioritizes extreme clarity, fast scanning, large tap targets, and functional status color-coding. Unnecessary decoration is stripped away in favor of high-contrast, structural precision.

grid_strategy.pos_screen: grid-cols-12 gap-4 with 8 cols for menu, 4 cols for cart

buttons.primary: bg-slate-900 text-white hover:bg-slate-800 rounded-md px-6 py-3 font-medium h-auto
buttons.secondary: bg-white text-slate-900 border border-slate-200 hover:bg-slate-50 rounded-md px-6 py-3 font-medium h-auto
buttons.danger: bg-red-600 text-white hover:bg-red-700 rounded-md px-6 py-3 font-medium h-auto

badges.default: inline-flex items-center px-2.5 py-0.5 rounded-full text-xs font-medium

image_urls.description: Restaurant interior for login screen background

iconography.size: w-5 h-5 for inline, w-8 h-8 for empty states

testing.data_testid_convention: kebab-case, role-based, required on all interactive elements

instructions_to_main_agent: Strictly follow the color palette, using aggregator brand colors (Zomato Red, Swiggy Orange) exclusively for their respective integrations.
Ensure all tap targets (buttons, menu items, table squares) have a minimum height of 48px to accommodate fast, imprecise tapping.
Use grid-cols-12 for the main POS layout: 8 columns for the menu grid and 4 columns for the active cart.
Implement clear visual distinctions for table states using the status colors defined in the palette.
Never use generic placeholder images. Use the provided Unsplash URLs.
Use Lucide React icons for all iconography.
Use standard Shadcn components for forms, tables, and dialogs, but style them with strict high-contrast borders and removing soft box-shadows.
Display a visible 'Offline Mode' badge in the header using the designated offline status color when applicable.
